facts.label: Present continuous e perfect
facts.sub: Agora: am/is/are + -ing. Já feito: have/has + particípio. Pergunta: Have you…?

facts.label: Está vazando
facts.sub: Use am, is ou are + verbo com -ing para falar do que acontece agora: The tap is leaking. Water is running on the floor. Em português, é “está vazando”. Não esqueça o verbo to be antes do -ing.

facts.label: Já chamei
facts.sub: O present perfect usa have ou has + particípio. Serve para o que você já fez e ainda importa hoje: I have called a plumber. Para verbos regulares, o particípio termina em -ed.

compare.ask: The tap is leaking, and I have called a plumber.
compare.br: No Brasil, usamos “está vazando” e “já chamei” de forma parecida.
compare.tip: Diga: “The tap is leaking, and I have called a plumber.”
compare.us: Em inglês, now pede am/is/are + -ing; o que já foi feito pede have/has + particípio.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The present continuous talks about now.
items.why: Yes, as in: the tap is leaking.

items.s: The present perfect uses have or has + participle.
items.why: Yes, as in: I have called.

items.s: “She has call a plumber” is correct.
items.why: We say: she has called a plumber.

answers: The present continuous talks about now. → Verdadeiro (Yes, as in: the tap is leaking.)
The present perfect uses have or has + participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes, as in: I have called.)
“She has call a plumber” is correct. → Falso (We say: she has called a plumber.)

pages.title: A leaking tap in Boston · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold evening in Boston. Lena lives in a small apartment with a green kitchen. For two weeks, she has had a problem with the tap. Today the water is running again. Her friend Bia is coming to help. Lena is waiting at the door.

“Bia, come in. The tap is leaking again, and the water is running onto the floor.” says Lena. “Oh no! Have you called a plumber yet?” says Bia. “Yes, I have called one, but he is working at another house today.” says Lena.
